correctness.rationale: For odd q, the ordered off-diagonal difference map (a,b)↦(a−b,a²−b²) has inverse a=(d+s/d)/2, b=(s/d−d)/2 when d≠0. All diagonals produce only (0,0). Thus character orthogonality on the complete q² sampling grid gives exactly J_q(A)=tr(A)²+sum_{a≠b}|A_ab|². Splitting Hermitian matrices orthogonally into scalar diagonal, traceless diagonal and off-diagonal gives real singular values sqrt(q) once, 0 (q−1) times and 1 q(q−1) times. Cauchy–Schwarz on the diagonal yields the upper bound; the corresponding nonnegative sum-of-squares defects give both iff equality cases, and a complex Hadamard conjugation realizes a flat diagonal for every prescribed spectrum. Rank-r projection gives r²≤J≤r²+r−r²/q for 1≤r≤q. I independently recomputed the character sum/Parseval identity on q=3,5,7 and inspected CHECK.py; prime tests alone do not prove the prime-power case, which follows algebraically from field invertibility of 2.
